summary: API gateway backpressure causing elevated 5xx rate and upstream runtime crashloops for tenant
summary_detail: Customer VectorRetail reports a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API beginning 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC. Errors correlate with elevated connection queue length at API gateway and rapid restarts of runtime pods serving the tenant's dedicated pool. Impacting production traffic for multiple storefront features; some requests see repeated 502/503 chains and streaming sessions drop mid-response.
description:
Issue summary:
- Elevated 5xx rate observed for tenant VectorRetail starting 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC, concentrated in us-east region.
- Symptoms: API gateway returning 502/503/504; long latencies followed by upstream connection resets; serving-runtime pods for the dedicated pool entering crashloop back-to-back.
Impact:
- Several VectorRetail storefront endpoints are erroring for end users and internal health checks. Estimated 25% error rate for requests routed to dedicated pool at peak.
Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated pool for VectorRetail).
- Model traffic: mix of redwood/open-8b-v1 and redwood/compat-4x-slim, mostly short chat completions and streaming.
Timeline (high level):
- 09:12 UTC: customer reports first errors.
- 09:15 UTC: Platform metrics show queue growth at API gateway and increased upstream 5xx.
- 09:18 UTC: Several runtime pods restarted; some pods repeatedly OOM or exit 137 within 30s of start.
- 09:30 UTC: SRE throttled incoming requests to the pool and engaged temporary rate-limiter to stabilize.
- 10:05 UTC: Partial stabilization after reducing concurrency and applying memory limit rollback on runtime image.
- 11:00 UTC: Customer still observes intermittent 502s during streaming sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a burst of concurrent streaming chat completion requests (50-100 parallel connections) to the VectorRetail tenant endpoint in prod-us-east.
2) Use payloads that request streaming with moderately long response (max_tokens ~1024) and frequent small chunks to encourage KV cache usage.
3) Observe API gateway queue length metric and per-route 5xx rate within 1-3 minutes.
4) Monitor serving-runtime pod logs for OOMs, kernel-fallback lines, and crashloop exit codes.
logs: 2026-03-14T09:17:03Z runtime-pod-7fdc OOMKilled: memory usage 14.8GB of 16GB allocated (exit_code=137)
2026-03-14T09:17:05Z runtime-pod-7fdc kernel: rtx memcpy fallback invoked for attention kernels
customer_message: We started seeing spikes of 502/503 around 09:10 UTC and a lot of our streaming sessions drop. This affects checkout preview and chat assistants. Please advise; we are on a marketing push today.
comments: 2026-03-14T09:20Z Support (Aisha Park): Acknowledged — opening incident and escalating to SRE. Collecting logs and metrics. Please share tenant request IDs if available.

2026-03-14T09:25Z SRE (Marco Liu): Noted high apigw queue_length and several runtime pod restarts; hypothesis: backpressure at gateway plus memory pressure on dedicated runtime leading to OOM crashloops. Pausing automated scale actions to prevent flapping.
2026-03-14T09:40Z Support (Aisha Park): Customer provided sample request IDs: r-vec-000124, r-vec-000130, r-vec-000145. Forwarded to SRE for trace lookup.

2026-03-14T10:00Z SRE (Marco Liu): Applied temporary mitigation: lowered per-tenant concurrency limit from 80->30, increased max_cached_prefix to reduce KV thrash, rolled back a recent runtime memory-change config. Seeing 5xx rate drop from 25%->8%.
2026-03-15T08:30Z Product (Priya Sharma): Noted this tenant was on a recent model variant rollout (compat-4x-slim) yesterday; we should verify kernel selection and quantization profile interactions.
2026-03-15T09:10Z SRE (Marco Liu): Running controlled soak with synthetic traffic; observing stable behavior with concurrency cap and reverted runtime mem config. Continuing monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-15T11:00Z Customer (VectorRetail - ops@vectorretail.com): Confirming improved behavior after throttling; still occasionally see a dropped streaming chunk ~1/min.
2026-03-15T11:30Z Support (Aisha Park): Scheduling follow-up call with VectorRetail to review traffic patterns and recommend batching/streaming knob adjustments.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Apigw queue pressure due to tenant burst + upstream slow kernel path causing long-lived connections and connection accumulation.
Observed frequent kernel-fallback messages in runtime logs indicating fallback from optimized attention kernel to slower memcpy-based path which increases CPU/memory pressure.
OOMs correspond to model variant memory allocation spikes; deduced that the recent runtime config lowered headroom for ephemeral tensors during streaming.
Autoscaler warmup was blocked by API-side rate limiting which prevented gradual scale-up and resulted in concentrated load on few pods, leading to thrashing.
No evidence of underlying hardware failure; GPU metrics per-node are within expected ranges but per-pod memory usage spikes correlate with long streaming sessions and KV cache misses.
root_cause: Combination of API gateway backpressure during a tenant burst, a recent runtime memory config change that reduced headroom for streaming workloads, and blocked autoscaler warmup due to rate-limiter interactions. These factors concentrated load on a small set of pods, causing OOMs and crashloops that amplified 5xx responses.
action_items: A) Revert the memory headroom change that reduced runtime ephemeral allocation (done 2026-03-14 09:50 UTC).
B) Adjust apigw per-tenant concurrency controls to smoother degradation policy and add circuit-breaker soft-queue limits (scheduled).
C) Add autoscaler rule to ignore short-term API rate-limit throttles during warmup or surface a warmup override for dedicated pools (investigating).
D) Run model-variant kernel-selection validation for compat-4x-slim under streaming workloads to identify quantization/kernel fallback triggers (P2 engineering task).
E) Follow-up with VectorRetail on recommended client-side rate limiting/backoff and batching best practices (scheduled call).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: lowered tenant concurrency cap and rolled back recent runtime mem config which reduced OOMs and runtime restarts. Applied increased KV cache size to reduce prefix thrashing.
Result: 5xx rate dropped from ~25% peak to sustained ~5-8% with most streaming sessions successful. Customer reported improved experience but occasional single-chunk drops persist (~1/min).
Permanent work items: implement apigw soft-queue circuit-breaker, autoscaler warmup override, and kernel-selection validation for the model variant. Assigned to SRE/Runtime/Platform teams.
Customer communication: committed to 48h monitoring window and follow-up meeting to review changes and traffic shaping recommendations.
Status: Incident partially mitigated — monitoring in progress until control changes are implemented and validated.
next_steps: Complete engineering action items B-D, validate with synthetic and customer traffic, and review post-incident in 72 hours. Owner: Marco Liu.
